title: NZ election eve poll watch: right’s lead slipping with Opportunity still the wild card
paragraphs: On the eve of New Zealand’s general election, final polls show the right retaining its lead, but with support continuing to shift towards the left, and the centrist Opportunity Party potentially holding the balance of power.
Right-wing parties (National, ACT and New Zealand First) led left-wing parties (Labour, the Greens and Te Pāti Māori) by 2.3 points in the final 1News-Verian poll.
The right also led by 5.3 points in the Curia poll for the Taxpayers’ Union and by 2.5 points in the Freshwater poll for The Post.
